pins.name: D3
pins.label: D3 (GPIO0)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. No onboard user button on this board (checked - see notes.txt); only a non-GPIO RESET button (SW1) is present

pins.name: TX
pins.label: TX (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D4
pins.label: GPIO2 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH at boot. Onboard LED (active-low, LED_BUILTIN) - confirmed via official schematic, see chipGpios note
Onboard LED (active-low) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: RX
pins.label: RX (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: D0
pins.label: D0 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. D1 Mini has an on-board resistor-divider giving A0 a 0-3.2V range (unlike the bare chip's native 0-1.0V) - see adc note below
